thread:
marco_sales: FYI Acme bumped their target to 4,200,000 tokens/day and wants p95 <250ms for chat. They asked for a committed proposal with clear autoscale rules, burst strategy (preferably cheaper), and a concise preheat/runbook we can hand to their infra team.

liz_sol: Quick converts: 4.2M tokens/day ~ 48.6 tokens/sec sustained. Peak hour ~1.5M tokens -> ~417 tokens/sec. For our rdl-13b-q profile we measure ~45-65 tps/GPU depending on batching and KV hit-rate. Using conservative 45 tps/GPU -> naive peak GPUs = 417/45 ~9.3 -> round to 10 GPUs.

nina_infra: Recommendation for commit packaging (presales-friendly): 8 reserved GPUs (baseline) + 3 burst GPUs (dedicated) + optional 2 spot GPUs for cost savings. This gives: baseline ~360 tps, +3 burst ~135 tps -> total ~495 tps headroom. Spot adds extra cushion but treat as reclaimable.

nina_infra: Important caveats: long-context sessions (50k+ tokens) and cold KV caches reduce effective tps. Plan for a 20-40% hit during initial warmup. Also memory-pressure-driven KV eviction can cause short-lived p95 spikes. We should document mitigations.

sam_prod: Autoscale recipe for the customer doc — hybrid triggers (token-rate + queue + memory):

```json
{
  "autoscale_strategy": "hybrid_token_queue_memory",
  "min_reserved_gpus": 8,
  "max_total_gpus": 13,
  "scale_triggers": {
    "token_rate_tps_above": 340,
    "queue_depth_ms_above": 120,
    "kv_memory_pressure_pct_above": 75
  },
  "scale_step": 1,
  "scale_cooldown_s": 60,
  "spot_fallback_fraction": 0.15
}
```

sam_prod: Notes: token_rate_tps_above uses an aggregated 30s moving average. When kv_memory_pressure_pct_above crosses threshold, prefer dedicated burst spin-ups over spot.

liz_sol: Preheat plan (customer-run routine): nightly passive prewarm + active preheat 30 minutes before expected surge. Passive: sample 1% of live traffic with a warmed context queue; Active: run synthetic requests for top 250 prompt templates and top 100 user-prefixes. Provide them a small script and cron example.

marco_sales: Pricing guidance for AE: propose 8-reserved + 3-burst committed band. Two options: (1) dedicated-heavy: 8R+3B at 12-month commit -> ~35% discount vs on-demand; (2) mixed: 8R+1B(dedicated)+2B(spot) -> ~45% blended saving but with spot risk. Add a table with monthly commit vs expected unit cost and burst allowances.

nina_infra: Operational SOW blurbs for failure modes: if burst exhausted -> soft-fallback to quantized lower-capacity model (approx +60ms median latency, quality delta noted in appendix). If whole pool down in an AZ, route to cross-AZ replicas (may incur +20-50ms network delta). Recommend 2-AZ placement and explicit cross-AZ failover clause.

marco_sales: Client-side recommendations to include in the security questionnaire/ops doc: surface X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-Backpressure-Delay(ms) headers, implement client-side exponential backoff + jitter, and soft degrade UI where possible (e.g., lower token count on retry).

sam_prod: Edge-case mitigation: concurrent large-context onboarding. Add per-session soft cap of 60k tokens and a token-rate throttle per session (e.g., 20 tps max) with clear client error 429 + Retry-After.

ops_bot: perf-summary.csv uploaded to #sales-assets (link: https://redwood.internal/sales-assets/perf-summary-2920001111.csv)

marco_sales: Action items: @liz_sol produce the one-page sizing + two pricing options; @nina_infra prepare the autoscale JSON + preheat scripts and a short failure-mode paragraph; @sam_prod write the SOW fallback/latency buckets. Target internal review by COB Monday. Will send the consolidated doc to Acme once greenlit. :thumbsup:
